MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  MARCH 4, 2019

  A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
  at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by CHAIR ZIGRANG.

  2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR led those in attendance in the Pledge of Allegiance

  3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Scott, Schachter, Yoo, Zigrang, Carman, Edler, Medawar

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  None

  STAFF PRESENT:  Planning Director Wahba, Sr. Planner Naughton, and
  Administrative Assistant Corea

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 4, 2019 AS
  PRESENTED.

  There being no objection, CHAIR ZIGRANG so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL SUCH
  ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6-A

  There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-20-18; APPLICANT: MS. SHEELA DERANIYALAGA;
  LOCATION: 19 DAPPLEGRAY LANE; DESCRIPTION: A request for a Neighborhood
  Compatibility Determination for a one-story addition and deck to an existing one-story, single
  family residence. A Minor Deviation is request for the one-story addition to be built along the
  existing building line that encroaches in to the legal nonconforming sideyard setback. A Grading
  Permit is required for removal of the existing tennis court and related facilities.

  Sr. Planner Naughton presented a summary of the staff report. This application began as an
  administrative case, however, after a site visit and further research of the property’s entitlement
  history, it was discovered that the sports court contained a nonconforming seating area and the
  sports court fencing was not permitted through the Special Use Permit process. The proposal

Planning Commission Meeting  1
Minutes, March 4, 2019
   which in includes the removal of the sports court will reduce the lot coverage to 21% from 38.7%.
  An 838 sq. ft. addition is being proposed, which will encroach into the legal non-conforming side
  yard setback which triggered the need for a Minor Deviation. Staff can support this request since
  the proposal will not increase the height of the highest existing roof ridge and will not be
  increasing the nonconforming side yard setback.

  Sr. Planner Naughton stated that a letter was received by staff after the agenda was distributed
  and a copy was provided to the Planning Commission. In the letter, the property owner at 17
  Dapplegray, is requesting that a condition of approval be added to require a 6’ high wood fence
  along the southern property line in lieu of the chain link fence in order to provide additional
  privacy.

  Sr. Planner Naughton stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve PA-
  20-18, subject to the conditions of approval, outlined in the staff report.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked the property owner if she would be willing to install a wood
  fence along the southern property line as requested by the property owner at 17 Dapplegray.

  Sheela Deraniyalaga, 19 Dapplegray, stated that she will honor the request and further stated
  that her plan is to install a block wall in a couple of years.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked about a gate to the bridle trail. Ms. Deraniyalaga stated
  that a 10’ wide gate is already part of the plan.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 20-18 SUBJECT TO THE REQUIREMENT
  THAT A WOOD FENCE BE INSTALLED AT THE SOUTHERN PROPERTY LINE.

  AYES:  Scott, Schachter, Yoo, Zigrang, Carman, Edler, Medawar
  NOES:
  ABSENT:
  ABSTAIN:

  Planning Director Wahba stated that there is a 20-day appeal period for this item.

  B.  RESIDENCES AT ROLLING HILLS COUNTRY CLUB RESIDENTIAL GUIDELINES

  Sr. Planner Naughton stated that design guidelines for the Residences at Rolling Hills Country
  Club is being provided to the commission for informational purposes and will be shared with the
  City Council.

  Improvements to the lots will be reviewed by the Architectural Review Committee (ARC) prior
  to advancing to the city for review. Staff requested a copy of the design guidelines in order for
  planning staff to be consistent in their review and to properly advise property owners on what
  improvements may be implemented. The design guidelines along with the ARC review will
  ensure that the backyard improvements are consistent with the RPD District, and do not prevent
  the city from enforcing building and safety, fire requirements, or any zoning requirements that
  may not have been captured in the design guidelines.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that there is a discrepancy on page 13, item 2.3 (third bullet
  point), “… setback 3’ minimum from the side property line”, and the picture shows a 1’ setback.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER commented that when reading through the design guidelines
  one gets the impression that the ARC has the final decision and it is not until the end of the
  guidelines where one would realize that the city may have rules/regulations that supersede the
  guidelines. Sr. Planner Naughton stated that the approval letter from the ARC does inform
  property owner’s that there is still a review required by the city, but mentioned that she will relay
  this to the Chadmar Group and ask that the city’s review requirement be added to the beginning
  of the document.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER expressed his concern with the documents reference to the
  ARC granting variances. Sr. Planner Naughton stated that staff also expressed their concern

Planning Commission Meeting  2
Minutes, March 4, 2019
   with the word “variance” in the document since it is not the same as the variance as defined in
  the city’s municipal code. However, they did not adhere to the recommendation.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if staff reviewed the photos since a property owner may
  get the impression that if they see it in the picture then it is okay. Sr. Naughton stated that staff
  did review them and some did not capture what the ARC would approve. CHAIR ZIGRANG
  suggested adding some language that the pictures are representational only and do not
  constitute approval.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR, Planning Director Wahba stated
  that these design guidelines are mainly for backyard improvements.

  VICE CHAIR CARMAN inquired about the plan for street trees and any view issues. Sr. Planner
  Naughton stated that in terms of view, she is unsure of the tree species and will relay the
  concern to Chadmar.

  VICE CHAIR CARMAN expressed her concern with their commitment to replacing the trees that
  existed on the project site. Sr. Planner Naughton agreed and stated that two landscape plans
  have been submitted and will make sure that the street trees were part of the plans. VICE
  CHAIR CARMAN asked staff to make sure that the required street trees are on all the plans.
  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE

  There being no objection, CHAIR ZIGRANG so ordered.

  8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  NONE

  9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  VICE CHAIR CARMAN stated that she attended the Community Workshop regarding the
  George F Canyon Nature Center site on Palos Verdes Drive East and Palos Verdes Drive North
  and provided an overview on the items discussed.

  VICE CHAIR CARMAN inquired about the “Butcher Park” project. Planning Director Wahba
  stated that the project may be delayed due to a recent request by MWD for a pipe re-lining
  project at the site.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR inquired about the Merrill Gardens project. Planning Director
  Wahba stated that it is about a year to completion. COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR expressed
  concern with the traffic being created by the construction vehicles parked on Bart Earle Way
  and Silver Spur Road.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER inquired about the Peninsula Pointe project. Planning Director
  Wahba stated that the project is in litigation.

  10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

  A.  Planning Director Wahba reminded the commissioners to submit form 700 by April 2, 2019.

  11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, FEBRUARY 12, 2019

  B.  DRAFT PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, FEBRUARY 19, 2019

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR CARMAN to,

   RECEIVE AND FILE ITEMS 11A – 11B

  There being no objection, CHAIR ZIGRANG so ordered

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR ZIGRANG adjourned the meeting at 7:40 p.m. to the next Planning Commission
  meeting on April 1, 2019.
